newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi to quit pachinko card business - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi to quit pachinko card business - paper.

text.p: Trading house Mitsubishi Corp will withdraw from the business of prepaid cards for "pachinko" pinball and will sell most of its shares in its pachinko card unit, a Japanese business daily said on Thursday.

Widespread card forgery has meant that the liabilities of Japan Leisure Card System Co -- which is 18.85 percent owned by Mitsubishi -- exceed its assets by 46 billion yen, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.

The unit is expected to post a net loss in the year to March 31, 1997, despite an estimated record nine trillion yen or more in sales, the paper said. The paper did not specify the amount of the estimated net loss.
Mitsubishi was not immediately available for comment.
The Nihon Keizai said Mitsubishi was looking for buyers for the unit"s shares among companies in the pachinko industry.

The paper said that the trading house was also pulling out of the business due to public criticism of trading companies for dealing in the pachinko industry as it has been associated with various social problems.
